app_summary: An online shop selling astronomy products, based on the OpenTelemetry Demo. It is built with polyglot microservices (Go, Java, .NET, Python, Node.js, Rust, ...) communicating via gRPC and HTTP behind an Envoy frontend-proxy, with Kafka for asynchronous order processing and Valkey as cart store. Supported Operations: View product catalog, Receive product recommendations and ads, Add item to cart, Checkout with selected items, Currency conversion, Process payment, Generate shipping quotes, Send order confirmation emails

symptoms.evidence: 10 error traces contain the same RPC error originating from payment/charge logic: "13 INTERNAL: failed to charge card: could not charge the card: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = dns: A record lookup error: lookup badAddress on 10.96.0.10:53: server misbehaving". rca_analyses_list.diagnosis: Checkout failures to charge cards are caused by DNS resolution failures for the external payment/charge host name 'badAddress' (A record lookup to cluster DNS 10.96.0.10:53 returns "server misbehaving"). This causes the payment gRPC calls to fail with code=Unavailable and the "dns: A record lookup error" message.
rca_analyses_list.reasoning: 1) Traces from checkout contain identical RPC errors: "13 INTERNAL: failed to charge card: ... rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = dns: A record lookup error: lookup badAddress on 10.96.0.10:53: server misbehaving" (multiple traceIDs provided). 2) The checkout pod is healthy and is configured to call the in-cluster payment service (PAYMENT_ADDR=payment:8080) — so checkout itself is not misconfigured. 3) The observed RPC error shows name resolution failed for host 'badAddress' against cluster DNS (10.96.0.10), indicating CoreDNS (or the cluster DNS path) is returning errors and preventing the payment attempt to the external host. These DNS lookup failures cause the payment/charge RPCs to return Unavailable and thus checkout cannot charge cards.

insights: Checkout service had a single running, Ready pod (checkout-6598d86d4b-gl85x) in namespace astronomy-shop.
Checkout pod environment shows PAYMENT_ADDR=payment:8080 — checkout is configured to call the in-cluster payment service, not a host named 'badAddress' (so checkout misconfiguration was disproven).
Payment service had a running, Ready pod (payment-6c5f448889-v5njb); its logs contained a MetadataLookupWarning and startup info but no pod crash.

Traces / error messages showed repeated gRPC failures: "13 INTERNAL: failed to charge card: ... rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = dns: A record lookup error: lookup badAddress on 10.96.0.10:53: server misbehaving" — indicating A-record DNS lookups for host 'badAddress' are failing against cluster DNS (10.96.0.10) with "server misbehaving".

Correlation: checkout -> payment RPCs fail with Unavailable because an attempted DNS A lookup for 'badAddress' (an external payment/charge host) fails at the cluster DNS layer; checkout is calling payment: payment (or payment code) attempts to resolve 'badAddress' and that lookup fails.

Root cause (immediate): DNS resolution failures for the external host 'badAddress' via the cluster DNS (CoreDNS / 10.96.0.10) — the DNS server returned "server misbehaving", causing gRPC Unavailable errors and failed card charges.

Unknown / unresolved: the investigation did not locate the exact configuration source that supplies the host name 'badAddress' (not visible in the pod env variables shown); it appears to be a runtime/external configuration or hardcoded value used by the payment component.
Impact: inability to resolve 'badAddress' caused payment operations to fail and propagated failed charge attempts back to checkout.

final_report.root_cause: A CoreDNS configuration error created a forwarding loop that caused cluster DNS to return SERVFAIL (“server misbehaving”), preventing application pods from resolving external hostnames. Specifically, the CoreDNS Corefile was configured with “forward . /etc/resolv.conf”, and the CoreDNS pods’ /etc/resolv.conf contained the cluster DNS IP (kube-dns ClusterIP 10.96.0.10). CoreDNS therefore forwarded queries back to the cluster DNS IP (itself), producing repeated DNS A-record lookup failures (seen as “lookup badAddress on 10.96.0.10:53: server misbehaving”). Those DNS failures caused payment-related gRPC calls to fail with code=Unavailable and propagated errors to checkout and frontend-proxy, causing card-charging failures.
final_report.evidence_summary: 1) Multiple application traces (traceIDs: 0df6b297..., 10477a37..., c8e603b2d...) show identical RPC errors: "13 INTERNAL: failed to charge card: ... rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = dns: A record lookup error: lookup badAddress on 10.96.0.10:53: server misbehaving". 2) checkout pod env contains PAYMENT_ADDR=payment:8080, disproving checkout DNS misconfiguration. 3) kube-dns Service ClusterIP is 10.96.0.10 — matching the DNS IP shown in the errors. 4) CoreDNS ConfigMap (Corefile) contains "forward . /etc/resolv.conf", so CoreDNS will forward to resolv.conf. 5) CoreDNS pods are Running/Ready and their /etc/resolv.conf resolves to 10.96.0.10, producing an effective forward-to-self (loop). 6) No application pod crashes were found; errors are consistent with cluster-level DNS SERVFAILs caused by the forwarding loop.
final_report.investigation_summary: Priority weighting: priority #1 investigation focused on checkout traces and pod state; priority #2 looked at cluster DNS. Steps performed: inspected traces and error messages, verified checkout pod config and logs, inspected payment pod logs, queried kube-system services/pods, retrieved CoreDNS ConfigMap (Corefile) and described CoreDNS pods. Correlated that the DNS failure IP in traces (10.96.0.10) is the kube-dns ClusterIP and that CoreDNS is forwarding to /etc/resolv.conf which contains that same IP — establishing a forwarding loop. This explains why external hostnames (e.g., 'badAddress') could not be resolved and why gRPC calls returned Unavailable, propagating failures through frontend-proxy to clients. The evidence chain is complete: trace errors → cluster DNS IP → CoreDNS Corefile misconfiguration → forwarding loop → SERVFAIL → application DNS failures.
